stem: $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ are two tangent segments drawn from the point $A$ to the circle $M$, where $B$ and $C$ are the points of tangency. If $m(\angle ABC) = {=x}^\circ$, find $m(\angle BMC)$.
solution: $AB = AC$ because they are tangent segments from $A$, so triangle $ABC$ is isosceles and $m(\angle ACB) = m(\angle ABC) = {=x}^\circ$.
The radii $MB$ and $MC$ are perpendicular to the tangents, so $m(\angle MBA) = m(\angle MCA) = 90^\circ$.
notes: Text-only; no figure needed. x in 50..80 gives angle A between 20 and 80. Answer in degrees (number only).
